title: Hey Krishna, hey friend
hook: Arjuna realizes his best friend is God, and remembers every joke he ever made
carry: god can be loved as a friend

segments.voice: Yesterday, kala: I am time is god's; i'm only the instrument, and be only the instrument. Your line was time is God's; I'm only the instrument. Today, Arjuna answers, trembling.

Your oldest friend, the one you've known forever. You've teased them, beaten them at cards, shared a bed on a camping trip, eaten off their plate without asking, called them ridiculous nicknames. Then one day you find out who they really are, and it's bigger than anything you ever imagined. Your first thought might not be wow. It might be: oh no. All those jokes. All those times I treated you like just anybody. That's exactly where Arjuna is in today's verses, trembling, palms pressed together.
screen: `YOUR OLDEST FRIEND.` → `THE TEASING, THE NICKNAMES.` → `OH NO. ALL THOSE JOKES.`

segments.voice: Sanjaya says Arjuna bows, trembling, and speaks with a choked voice. First, praise. It's right that the world rejoices in you and loves you. The frightened spirits flee in every direction, and the perfected ones bow. You are the first god, the ancient person, the final resting place of the universe. You are wind, death, fire, the moon, the father of all creatures. Then: bowing to you a thousand times, and again, and again. Bowing in front, bowing behind, bowing on every side. Then the confession, verses forty-one and forty-two. Thinking you were just my friend, I called you rashly: hey Krishna, hey Yadava, hey friend. I didn't know how great you were. Out of carelessness, or out of love, whatever disrespect I showed you as a joke, while playing, resting, sitting or eating, alone or in front of others, I ask you to forgive it, immeasurable one. Verse forty-four: bear with me as a father with a son, a friend with a friend, a lover with the beloved. Notice: he asks not for distance, but for the closeness to hold. And verse forty-five: I'm thrilled to have seen what no one has seen, and my mind is shaking with fear. Please, show me the form I know. Terror and praise, both at once. And a Hindu teaching lives right here: God can be loved as a friend. The Bhagavata Purana counts sakhya, friendship, among nine forms of devotion, and teachers often name Arjuna as its example. Many Hindus still end a puja asking pardon for any slip, then talk to God like family.
screen: `TREMBLING, HE BOWS.` · `A THOUSAND TIMES, ON EVERY SIDE.` · `HEY KRISHNA, HEY FRIEND.` · `AS A FRIEND WITH A FRIEND.` · then, large: `GOD, LOVED AS A FRIEND.`

segments.voice: If you pray, speak to God for a minute the way Arjuna once did: plainly, as a friend, by whatever name is yours. Then, as many Hindus do at the end of puja, ask pardon for any careless word, and ask the closeness to stay. If you don't pray, do the same in your heart for someone you've treated like just anybody.
Sakha. Friend, companion. Sakhya, friendship with God, is one of the forms of devotion. Seeing his friend as God, he bows a thousand times, and asks forgiveness for every careless word.
Your line: God can be loved as a friend. Hey Krishna, hey friend: the names he used before he knew. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Arjuna's hymn of praise in Gita 11.36–46 is recited by many Hindus in worship; sakhya, loving God as a friend, is one of the nine forms of devotion in the Bhagavata Purana, and many Hindus close a puja with a prayer asking pardon for any mistake or disrespect.

original.note: Sanskrit: sakha, friend, companion; 'he sakhe', hey friend, is one of the names Arjuna regrets (11.41).

trapdoor: what you thought: once you see how great God is, the friendship is over.
what it means: Arjuna trembles and praises, asks forgiveness for his familiarity, and asks the closeness to stay.

what a scholar hears: 11.41's 'he krishna he yadava he sakheti' lists the casual names Arjuna used; 11.44 names three bonds (father and son, friend and friend, lover and beloved); the Bhagavata Purana (7.5.23) lists sakhya, friendship, among nine forms of devotion.
